Near-term rates and the one-year path

At the decision release, asset prices can move with both the short rate and the expected path of future rates. Each coefficient estimates the asset change associated with a 5 bp increase in one instrument while the other is held fixed.

Across 176 Fed announcements, a 5 bp increase in one-year OIS was associated with a 5.73 bp rise in the two-year Treasury yield when the current-meeting surprise was held fixed.

Did the press conference reverse the initial move?

Compare the signed change in one-year OIS during the announcement with its change during the press conference on the same date.

In 21 of 35 Fed meetings where one-year OIS moved more than 1 bp in both windows, the press-conference move ran in the opposite direction.

How to read a meeting

Start with the policy decision and the market move already priced. Check whether the central bank changed its forecast for growth, inflation or the policy rate, and record when the projection became public. Then compare the release window with the press conference. An article published later can describe both.

Fed · 21 September 2022

Participants raised their median end-2023 policy rate from 3.8% in June to 4.6%. One-year OIS rose 8.47 bp around the announcement and fell 3.49 bp during the press conference. The Wall Street Journal highlighted the third consecutive 75 bp increase. Its headline supplied the size of the current action, while the projections quantified the change in the expected policy path.

September projectionsMeeting price windowsWSJ coverage

ECB · 15 December 2022

Eurosystem staff raised their 2023 inflation projection from 5.5% in September to 6.3% and lowered real GDP growth from 0.9% to 0.5%. One-year euro OIS rose 3.46 bp around the release and another 11.51 bp during the press conference. The staff projections describe the economic outlook. The OIS windows show how markets repriced during communications that also included the rate decision and policy guidance.
